chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the People of the Book. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, they do not eat your slaughters, so how do you permit yourselves to eat their slaughters? It is merely the name (Bismillah), and none can be relied upon regarding it except a Muslim.'

key_terms.أَهْل الْكِتَاب: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: Why are Muslims permitted to eat the slaughter of the People of the Book according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs a rhetorical argument of reciprocity, noting that since the People of the Book do not invoke Allah’s name over their meat, they do not truly partake in the blessed slaughters of Muslims. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the validity of their slaughter is contingent upon the actual recitation of the divine name, which is reliably performed only by Muslims. The hadith underscores the theological principle that the sanctity of the food is derived from the monotheistic invocation rather than merely the status of the slaughterer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a slaughter by the People of the Book. So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! They are not eating from your slaughters, so how are you permitting yourselves that you eat their slaughters? But rather, it is the naming (Bismillah), and none can be relied over it except for a Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the animals the people of the book slaughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘By Allah they do not eat what you slaughter; then how can you consider what they slaughter as lawful? It is a matter of name (mentioning the name of Allah), and no one can be trusted in it except a Muslim.’”
